spawn_spec.prompt:
TASK: Determine whether PowerPoint COM automation can be made a RELIABLE, REPEATABLE golden oracle on this Windows machine, and deliver either a working repeatable script or a precise, evidence-backed blocking condition. This is an executable investigation assignment, not a context handoff.

BACKGROUND (verified facts — trust these, do not re-derive):
- The agent shell runs in Windows SESSION 0 (non-interactive, services session). `[System.Environment]::UserInteractive` is False and `(Get-Process -Id $PID).SessionId` is 0.
- The user's real desktop is SESSION 1 (`query session` shows `rdp-tcp#0  steve  1  활성/Active`).
- Session 0 isolation is why PowerPoint COM fails there: `New-Object -ComObject PowerPoint.Application` succeeds and `Presentations.Add()` works, but `Presentations.Open(<path>)` throws OutOfMemoryException (0x8007000E) because PowerPoint needs a window station/desktop to open a document.
- Escaping to session 1 WORKS via a scheduled task with an interactive token:
    schtasks /create /tn <name> /tr "\"<path-to.cmd>\"" /sc once /st 23:59 /it /f
    schtasks /run /tn <name>
  The /tr value is limited to 261 characters, so point it at a small .cmd wrapper.
- PowerShell 5.1 reads .ps1 files as ANSI: a UTF-8 script WITHOUT a BOM containing Korean text fails to parse. Write .ps1 files as UTF-8 WITH BOM (Python: encoding="utf-8-sig"), or keep them pure ASCII.
- Office is Microsoft 365 Apps (O365ProPlusRetail), Click-to-Run, x64, version 16.0.20228.20190. PowerPoint is at C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\POWERPNT.EXE.
- From session 1, these outcomes were all observed across five different approaches:
    * ONE run fully succeeded: opened a 3-slide deck, exported `adversarial-slide-1.png` via Slide.Export(png,"PNG",1920,1080), read Shapes.Count.
    * Other runs failed with: RPC_E_CALL_REJECTED (0x80010001) including "서버 실행 파일이 CLSID를 등록하지 않았습니다"; MK_E_UNAVAILABLE (0x800401E3) from [Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::GetActiveObject("PowerPoint.Application"); and a null COM object right after CreateObject.
    * A retry helper that retries ONLY on RPC_E_* with 30-150 attempts was already used; it helped but did not make runs deterministic.
    * `$app.Visible = -1` (msoTrue) was required before Open succeeded in the run that worked.
    * Killing leftover POWERPNT.EXE between runs and pre-launching POWERPNT.EXE then attaching did NOT make it deterministic.

YOUR GOAL: run this down empirically and report a definitive verdict.

DELIVERABLE — write your artifacts under this directory (create it): C:\Users\steve\Desktop\projects\impromptu-r2\.omo\scratch\golden-oracle\
1. `probe-report.md` — your findings: what you ran, what happened each time, and the VERDICT: either
   (a) RELIABLE: a repeatable procedure with a measured success rate over at least 8 consecutive runs, or
   (b) BLOCKED: the exact blocking condition with the concrete error evidence and why no available action fixes it without user intervention.
2. If RELIABLE: `run-golden.cmd` + `golden.ps1` (UTF-8 with BOM or pure ASCII) that, given a .pptx path, opens it, exports each slide to PNG at 1920x1080, dumps every animation effect (index, Shape.Name, Shape.Id, EffectType as int, Timing.TriggerType as int, Timing.Duration as double) to `golden.json`, closes cleanly, and writes `status.txt` containing OK or FAIL. It must be runnable end-to-end by: `schtasks /run /tn <name>` and must leave no POWERPNT.EXE process behind.
3. If RELIABLE: evidence of at least 8 consecutive successful runs (a log with timestamps + the produced PNG/JSON file listings).

TEST DECK to use: C:\Users\steve\AppData\Local\Temp\impromptu-render-qa\korean-adversarial.pptx
(3 slides; slide 2 carries 3 animation effects: fade entrance on shape id 2, motion entrance on shape id 3, colour emphasis on shape id 2, plus a fade slide transition.)
If that file is missing, regenerate any 2-3 slide pptx with python-pptx using this interpreter:
C:\Users\steve\Desktop\projects\impromptu-r2\services\ingestion\.venv\Scripts\python.exe

INVESTIGATION ANGLES worth trying (pick what the evidence supports; you are not limited to these):
- Whether a COM message filter (IMessageFilter / OleMessageFilter registered via Add-Type C# in PowerShell) makes RPC_E_CALL_REJECTED disappear — this is the textbook fix for exactly that HRESULT and has NOT been tried yet.
- Whether opening with `WithWindow=msoFalse` after `$app.Visible=-1` behaves differently from `WithWindow=msoTrue`.
- Whether PowerPoint needs its first-run/licensing state settled (check HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Office\16.0\PowerPoint\ and whether a "recover files"/AutoRecovery dialog is pending; AutoRecovery items live under %APPDATA%\Microsoft\PowerPoint\).
- Whether disabling COM add-ins for the automation run stabilises it.
- Whether a fixed inter-run cooldown (process fully exited + a bounded wait for the CLSID to deregister) is what makes it deterministic.
- Whether `Presentations.Open2007(..., msoFalse)` or opening a COPY of the deck in a trusted location behaves better than Open on the original.

HARD RULES:
- Every run MUST go through the scheduled-task interactive-token path; session 0 cannot open decks and re-proving that is a waste.
- Use a task name distinct from anything else: `ImpromptuGoldenProbe`. DELETE it when you finish (`schtasks /delete /tn ImpromptuGoldenProbe /f`) and confirm deletion.
- Kill stray POWERPNT.EXE processes when you finish; the machine must be left clean. Report the cleanup commands you ran and their output.
- The user is actively using session 1. Do NOT run a fullscreen slideshow, do NOT leave PowerPoint windows open, and keep each run short.
- NEVER run git commit/add or any git write command.
- Do NOT modify any file outside .omo\scratch\golden-oracle\ .
- Report `WORKING: <phase>` before long run batches; report `BLOCKED: <reason>` only if you truly cannot proceed.

VERIFY before reporting: if you claim RELIABLE, you must paste the log of 8 consecutive successful runs. If you claim BLOCKED, you must paste the exact error text (HRESULT + message) from at least 3 distinct approaches you tried.

STOP WHEN: probe-report.md exists with a definitive RELIABLE or BLOCKED verdict backed by pasted run evidence, the scheduled task is deleted, no POWERPNT.EXE remains, and you have reported the verdict plus the artifact paths.
